title: Ham or pork with noodles and vegetables in tomato sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of ham or lean pork, boiled noodles, vegetables (carrots, broccoli and/or dark‑green leafy greens) and a tomato‑based sauce. It combines protein, complex carbohydrates and vitamins for a balanced meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, studied for its potential anti‑cancer properties.
Noodles made from hard wheat retain more protein than those from soft wheat.
Ham is often smoked, giving it a distinctive flavor and extending shelf life.
The protein‑carbohydrate combo improves amino‑acid uptake after physical activity.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Ham and pork provide complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and noodles supply thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Vitamin C and antioxidants
items.content: Tomato sauce and broccoli deliver vitamin C, which boosts immune function.

items.title: Fiber and minerals
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain noodles add dietary fiber, potassium and magnesium, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Tomatoes provide fiber and mild probiotic effects, while vegetables stimulate gut motility.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham often contains high levels of salt; people with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Pork can be high in saturated fat, which may increase cardiovascular risk if consumed excessively.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato products.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Tomato sauce may contain added sugar and preservatives; choose versions without added sugar when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, tossing noodles with sauce, meat and vegetables. Garnish with fresh herbs (basil, oregano) or a sprinkle of grated cheese for extra flavor. It works well as a post‑workout meal or a family dinner.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For freezing, store up to 2 months after cooling. Reheat to at least 75 °C before eating. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
